general.description: Core router configuration: whether it's active, its hostname, and timezone.

enabled.description: Toggle the router service on/off (e.g., disables routing if false).

hostname.description: Fully-qualified domain name of the router (used in logs, banners, and some DNS contexts).

timezone.description: System timezone (must be a valid IANA timezone name like 'UTC' or 'America/New_York').

interfaces.description: Network interface assignments: external (WAN) and internal (LAN), plus optional extra LAN interfaces.

lan_interface.description: Name of the primary internal (LAN) interface.

lan_extra.description: List of additional LAN interface names (e.g., for VLANs, guest networks, or multi-site branches).

ipam.description: IP address management for the LAN: subnet, DHCP range, lease duration, and DNS servers to advertise.

lan_subnet.description: IPv4 network for the LAN in CIDR notation (e.g., '192.168.1.0/24').

lan_dhcp_start.description: First IP address in the DHCP address pool.

lan_dhcp_end.description: Last IP address in the DHCP address pool.

lan_dhcp_lease_time.description: DHCP lease duration in seconds (e.g., 86400 = 24 hours).

lan_dns_servers.description: Ordered list of DNS servers to advertise via DHCP (router’s IP is typically first).

nat.description: NAT rules: enables outbound masquerading and optional port forwarding rules.

enabled.description: Enable NAT for outbound traffic (required for internet access behind the router).

masquerade_interface.description: Interface to use for masquerading (usually same as WAN interface).

enable_port_forwarding.description: Enable static port forwarding (requires manual port_forward rules to be defined).

external_port.description: Port exposed on the router (WAN side).

internal_port.description: Destination port on the internal host.

port_forwards.description: List of port forwarding rules (each maps an external port to an internal host/port).

firewall.description: Basic firewall policy: default deny incoming, plus exceptions for specific services.

default_deny_in.description: Block all unsolicited inbound connections unless explicitly allowed.

allow_established.description: Permit inbound packets that are part of existing, outbound-initiated sessions.

allow_loopback.description: Allow local loopback traffic (required for local services).

name.description: Well-known service name (e.g., 'ssh', 'http', 'https', 'dns') or port number.

interfaces.description: List of interfaces on which to allow this service (e.g., ['lan', 'eth1']).

allowed_services.description: List of services to explicitly allow inbound (e.g., SSH for remote management).

ntp.description: NTP client settings: upstream server and whether NTP is active.

server.description: Primary NTP server (can be a domain or IP).

enabled.description: Enable NTP time synchronization on the router.

logging.description: System logging configuration: verbosity and output target.

level.description: Minimum log level to record (debug = most verbose).

log_target.description: Where to send logs: 'syslog' (for journald/rsyslog) or 'file' (uses backup.log_dir as fallback path).

backup.description: Automatic configuration backup: enable, location, retention, and frequency.

enabled.description: Enable scheduled backups of the router config.

backup_dir.description: Local directory to store config backups (must be writable).

max_backups.description: Number of recent backup files to retain (older ones are deleted).

monitoring.description: Built-in service health monitoring: interval, timeout, and services to watch.

health_checks.description: Enable periodic health checks for critical services (e.g., DHCP, DNS, firewall).

interval_seconds.description: Seconds between health check cycles (must be ≥10).

service_timeout.description: Seconds to wait before declaring a monitored service as down.

protocol.description: Check protocol: 'tcp' (simple port check) or 'http' (HTTP request).

host.description: Host to check (for 'http', use 'localhost' or '127.0.0.1'; for TCP, use IP or hostname).

path.description: URL path for HTTP checks (ignored for TCP).

expect_status.description: Expected HTTP status code (used only for HTTP checks).

monitored_services.description: List of services to monitor (e.g., internal HTTP admin interface, local DNS resolver).
